subject: Invoice on hold — unusual embed consumption (requesting breakdown)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerly.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@ledgerly.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice on hold — unexpected embeddings spike

Soojin,

We placed the latest invoice (Aug cycle) on hold because our finance team flagged a 3.7x jump in embeddings consumption between July 28–30. The invoice reference is INV-2026-08-01. The charge line reads: "Embeddings (production) — 2,340,000 units" which is far higher than our historical ~620k/week average.

We haven't changed any batch sizes on our side and we aren't running bulk reindex jobs. Can you provide: 1) a per-day unit breakdown for that period, 2) the exact counting method used for embeddings (are we billed per embed request or per vector chunk?), and 3) any known platform changes that could inflate counts (tokeniser changes, sampling, retry accounting)?

We need the breakdown to clear the payment hold by Monday; otherwise procurement will escalate and delay the payment. Attaching our snapshot export and the invoice.

Thanks —
Daniel
VP of Finance, Ledgerly
[Attachment: usage_snapshot_ledgerly_20260801.csv] [Attachment: invoice_20260801.pdf]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerly.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — unexpected embeddings spike

Daniel —

Thanks for flagging this and sharing the snapshot. I'm sorry for the disruption; we want to get this resolved quickly so payment can proceed. Quick answers up front: 1) Redwood bills embeddings per request-response pair (per embedding call) with an internal normalization for batched calls — we do not split a single logical embed call into multiple billed units unless the request exceeded model input-size and had to be sharded. 2) We did not push a tokeniser change during that window. 3) There was a short-lived caching regression on 2026-07-29 that could have caused duplicate backend requests in certain retry edge-cases — engineering is investigating correlation with your account.

We're compiling the per-day breakdown now. Aditya, can you pull the shard-level export for acct HW-4893 and check for duplicate request-ids / replays between 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-30? Marissa — I'll need a quick billing recalculation draft (per-day) we can send to Ledgerly.

I'll follow up with the CSV export and a short reconciliation table in ~3 hours.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inc.

On Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 10:15 AM Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerly.com> wrote:
> Soojin,
> 
> We placed the latest invoice (Aug cycle) on hold because our finance team flagged a 3.7x jump...

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — shard export + findings (HW-4893)

Soojin / Marissa —

I pulled the per-shard export for HW-4893 (attached redwood_export_ids.txt) and matched request-ids against our ingestion logs. Findings:
- 2026-07-28: 612,412 credited embed units (baseline)
- 2026-07-29: 1,987,910 billed embed units — 78% of these share identical request_ids and timestamps indicating a replay loop.
- 2026-07-30: 1,739,640 billed units — majority are from batched replays across three worker slots.

Root cause appears to be a brief caching invalidation combined with a retry policy that retriggered batch jobs; in some cases the client-side request was retried and the retry header was not forwarded by an older SDK shim, so the platform recorded them as new requests. This matches ledgerly's CSV where many rows show similar payload hashes.

Suggested remediation: issue a retroactive credit for duplicate request_ids between 2026-07-29 02:00:00 UTC and 2026-07-30 23:59:59 UTC. I can provide a deduplicated per-request export for Marissa to use in recalculation.

Attaching: redwood_export_ids.txt (list of request ids and timestamps).

— Aditya
Infra Engineer — Billing Systems

[Attachment: redwood_export_ids.txt]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerly.com>
Cc: finance@ledgerly.com, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — reconciliation and corrected statement (INV-2026-08-01)

Daniel —

Thank you for your patience. We've completed the reconciliation and applied a retroactive credit for duplicate embed requests during the window we identified. Summary:
- Original billed embeds (2026-07-28 to 2026-07-30): 5,965,962 units
- Duplicate request_ids identified and removed: 3,167,402 units
- Net billable embeds after dedupe: 2,798,560 units
- Credit applied: USD 18,392.10 (appears as line CREDIT-REFUND on your updated invoice)

Actions taken:
- Billing adjustment posted; updated invoice attached (invoice_20260801.pdf — v2).
- We've updated the SDK shim and pushed a fix to ensure retry headers are preserved; that'll prevent missing dedupe IDs in the future.
- Engineering has a postmortem scheduled; we will share the public summary and mitigation timeline by end of next week.

Next steps for ledgerly: 1) Please confirm receipt of the updated invoice and whether the credit and new total resolve the payment hold; 2) If you want a CSV with the deduplicated request-level rows we used for the adjustment, reply and we'll provide it (redacted payloads).

Thanks again — apologies for the disruption. We're happy to expedite any additional evidence your finance team needs.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: invoice_20260801.pdf]
